title: Feed-forward network: d → m → d with a nonlinear bend
why: It shows the two-matrix pipeline and where the activation sits, including the residual add and the collapse without a bend.
notes: Left-to-right dataflow: a d-dimensional residual vector enters W₁, widens to the intermediate width m, passes through the coordinatewise nonlinearity, and W₂ projects back to d; the result is added to the residual stream. The only labelled quantities are the structural widths d and m from the prose. Without the activation, W₂W₁ composes into a single d→d matrix, so the intermediate width buys no expressive power. | x-axis is input x; y-axis is activation value and derivative value. Plot GELU(x) and its derivative, marking the chapter's points: x=0 gives GELU=0 and derivative 0.5; x=1 gives GELU=0.8413 and derivative 1.0833; x=-1 gives GELU=-0.1587 and derivative -0.0833; x=-2 gives GELU=-0.0455 and derivative -0.0852; x=-3 gives GELU=-0.0040 and derivative -0.0119; x=-4 derivative about -0.0005. A ReLU reference can show zero output and zero derivative for negative x, contrasting with GELU's small nonzero negative-side derivative. | Left-to-right flow: x feeds both W_g and W_v. W_g output passes through sigmoid to become a soft switch between 0 and 1; W_v output passes through unchanged. The two d×m branches are multiplied elementwise; the product is what W_d sees. The up-projection W₁ is d×2m and is split into W_g and W_v, each d×m. No numerical values beyond the chapter's d, m, and 2m are labelled. | Dataflow: x feeds two separate projections; gate branch applies Swish or sigmoid; value branch stays linear; branches multiply elementwise; result projects down. Label model width d and intermediate width m. Compare plain FFN: two d×4d matrices, 8d² parameters and multiply-adds per token. Gated FFN: three d×m matrices; holding 8d² requires 3dm=8d², so m=8d/3≈2.67d; leaving m=4d gives 12d², a 50% FFN parameter increase. All quantities come from the chapter. | Left side compares bias counts: plain FFN at 5d versus gated FFN at 19d/3 ≈ 6.33d, showing the gated layer has slightly more parameters when biases are present. Right side shows the intermediate-width rounding for d=4096: exact 10922.67, kernel-friendly 11008, a 0.78% increase. All quantities are from the chapter; no axes require invented values.
